evidence.source: executor command audit: disk inspection commands
evidence.finding: node1's only disk (vda, 20GiB) is fully partitioned (BIOS boot, /boot, swap, /) with zero free space — no spare disk/partition exists for a native LVM PV. This forced the executor onto a loopback-file-backed PV under /var/lib/lvm-backing/data.img on the root filesystem.

evidence.source: executor command audit: LV creation/grow step
evidence.finding: LV was created at 1GiB, populated with 50x1MiB files + checksum manifest, grown online to 2.5GiB via lvextend+xfs_growfs while mounted, and sha256sum -c passed both before and after the grow. This portion of the task (create + grow + integrity) is well-evidenced and appears successful.

evidence.source: executor command audit: persistence unit content
evidence.finding: datavg-loop.service was written with DefaultDependencies=no, Before=local-fs-pre.target, Conflicts=umount.target, and the fstab entry uses x-systemd.requires=datavg-loop.service. The full fstab line was redacted ('...[content omitted]...'), so it is unconfirmed whether the /srv/data mount option list includes nofail.
Boot ID was captured pre-reboot (739c9792-...) and a pre-reboot umount/remount rehearsal via fstab succeeded, showing the mount+checksum path worked in the running (not-yet-rebooted) kernel.

Every poll after 'systemctl reboot' (at +~2min, +~2min, +~3min, continuing to 90+ minutes per the report) returned 'Connection reset by peer' with return_code -1 — never a successful reconnect, never a changed boot_id.
Executor explicitly reports the restart-and-recover requirement as NOT satisfied rather than assuming success, and did not attempt to fabricate console access or bypass the no-TTY constraint.

likely_causes.cause: Boot-time dependency race/failure between the custom loop-reattach unit and LVM autoactivation for the generated /srv/data mount unit, escalating to emergency mode because the fstab entry likely lacks 'nofail' — and emergency mode requires interactive console access, which the exec tool cannot provide (no TTY per platform contract), making the node appear permanently unreachable even though it may be sitting at a rescue prompt.

DefaultDependencies=no on datavg-loop.service combined with Before=local-fs-pre.target may run the unit before the loop kernel module/udev/LVM subsystem is fully ready, causing the service itself to fail at boot and cascade into a failed local-fs.target if the mount is required (non-nofail).

Ordinary VM boot delay or transient platform/network issue unrelated to the LVM/systemd configuration (e.g., host-level hiccup). Cannot be ruled out without console/journal access to node1, but 90+ minutes is far outside any normal boot window described in the platform reference (which cites 5-10s for DHCP settling), making this less likely than a boot-blocking configuration issue.

The reboot command itself did not execute as intended (e.g., backgrounding trick silently failed before systemctl reboot ran), leaving node1 in an ambiguous state that is neither the old boot nor a new one. Less likely since the executor evidence shows the acknowledgement returned pre-disconnect, but not independently verifiable.

next_attempt_guidance: Use the same loopback-file-backed PV approach again if node1 on the fresh cluster has the same fully-partitioned 20GiB disk — this part of the task (create LV, mount at /srv/data, grow online to 2.5G+, verify checksums) was executed correctly and is a valid pattern given the disk constraint.

Add 'nofail,x-systemd.device-timeout=30' (or similar) to the /etc/fstab options for /srv/data so a mount failure at boot degrades to a failed mount unit instead of dropping the whole boot into an emergency shell that the exec tool cannot reach.

Simplify or remove DefaultDependencies=no / Conflicts=umount.target from the loop-reattach systemd unit unless there is a specific, tested reason for them; prefer standard ordering (After=systemd-udevd.service, Before=local-fs.target is generally safer than local-fs-pre.target) and validate with 'systemd-analyze verify' before relying on it across a reboot.

Before issuing the real reboot, dry-run the boot dependency chain non-destructively if possible (e.g., 'systemctl list-dependencies local-fs.target', check 'systemctl is-enabled datavg-loop.service', and confirm 'losetup', LVM activation, and the mount unit ordering with 'systemd-analyze plot' or dependency listing) to catch ordering problems before they can strand the node.

After issuing the reboot, poll on a shorter, escalating cadence (e.g., 15s for the first 2-3 minutes) rather than long sleeps, so a hang is detected quickly and can be reported as blocked well before 90 minutes elapse.

If the node becomes unreachable post-reboot for longer than ~5-10x the normal boot window cited in the platform primer, treat it as a likely boot-hang (not 'still booting') and report as blocked promptly rather than continuing to poll for over an hour, since exec has no TTY/console fallback to recover from an emergency shell.

Report explicitly (as this executor did) when restart-and-recovery verification cannot be completed rather than inferring success from pre-reboot rehearsal alone — the pre-reboot umount/remount test is not equivalent evidence to an actual kernel reboot.
summary: The core LVM task (loopback-backed PV, 1GiB LV mounted at /srv/data, grown online to 2.5GiB, data integrity verified before and after) was completed and well-evidenced. The attempt is blocked solely on the mandatory restart-and-recover verification: after 'systemctl reboot' on node1, the exec tool never reconnected over 90+ minutes, consistently returning 'Connection reset by peer'. Based on the redacted evidence alone, the most plausible explanation is a boot-time failure in the custom systemd persistence unit (loop device reattachment before LVM activation) combined with a possibly non-'nofail' fstab entry, which would drop the boot into an emergency shell unreachable via the no-TTY exec tool — but this cannot be confirmed without boot logs or console access, which are unavailable for this cluster. A platform-level VM/network failure unrelated to the configuration cannot be fully ruled out either. The executor correctly reported this as an unverified/blocked outcome rather than claiming success.</summary>
